translationRepairs: Hu Linyi, defending Liping, came to rely heavily on him and recommended him to Governor Jiang Yuanyuan, and Chao won fame from that time.
Hu Linyi, defending Liping, came to rely heavily on him and recommended him to Governor Jiang Weiyuan, and Chao won fame from that time.
The source names 蔣霨遠. The character 霨 is read Wei, so Jiang Weiyuan corrects the mistransliterated given name.
Hu Linyi was defending Liping and relied on him deeply; he spoke of him to Governor Jiang Yuanyuan, and Chao thereby became well known.
Hu Linyi was defending Liping and relied on him deeply; he spoke of him to Governor Jiang Weiyuan, and Chao thereby became well known.
The literal translation contains the same mistransliteration of 蔣霨遠; Jiang Weiyuan follows the source characters.

He stormed rebel strongholds at Xiangguping in Sinan, Tudituping in Shibing, and Jindingnao, Fengyannao, and Tangjiayingnao in Zhenyuan, captured bandit chiefs Zhang Dongshan and Ou Guangyi among others, and pacified the whole Zhenyuan region.

He stormed rebel strongholds at Xiangguping in Sizhou, Tudituping in Shibing, and Jindingnao, Fengyannao, and Tangjiayingnao in Zhenyuan, captured bandit chiefs Zhang Dongshan and Ou Guangyi among others, and pacified the whole Zhenyuan region.
The place in the source is 思州, Sizhou, not 思南, Sinan.

He suppressed the rebel nests at Xiangguping in Sinan, Tudituping in Shibing, and Jindingnao, Fengyannao, and Tangjiayingnao in Zhenyuan, captured the bandit leaders Zhang Dongshan, Ou Guangyi, and others, and pacified all districts under Zhenyuan.

He suppressed the rebel nests at Xiangguping in Sizhou, Tudituping in Shibing, and Jindingnao, Fengyannao, and Tangjiayingnao in Zhenyuan, captured the bandit leaders Zhang Dongshan, Ou Guangyi, and others, and pacified all districts under Zhenyuan.
The literal translation also misidentifies 思州 as Sinan; Sizhou is the source place name.
Provincial Military Commander Tian Xingyu memorialized Chao's battle record; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer and the title Wuyong Batulu.
Provincial Military Commander Tian Xingyu memorialized Chao's battle record; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer and the title Wuyong Baturu.
巴圖魯 is the established Manchu title Baturu; Batulu is not the intended English form.
Provincial Military Commander Tian Xingyu memorialized Chao's successive battle merits; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer and granted the title Wuyong Batulu.
Provincial Military Commander Tian Xingyu memorialized Chao's successive battle merits; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer and granted the title Wuyong Baturu.
The literal field contains the same incorrect form for 巴圖魯; Baturu is the established title.

In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baojing. Xingyu led forty-five hundred men to hold Jiugong Bridge and fought daily for more than a month until supplies ran low. He picked volunteers for a decisive battle, then Li Xuyi's relief force arrived. Inner and outer columns struck together, destroyed three camps by the walls, and swept the rest aside in days.

In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing. Xingyu led forty-five hundred men to hold Jiugong Bridge and fought daily for more than a month until supplies ran low. He picked volunteers for a decisive battle, then Li Xuyi's relief force arrived. Inner and outer columns struck together, destroyed three camps by the walls, and swept the rest aside in days.
The besieged city is 寶慶, Baoqing, rather than 寶靖, Baojing.

In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baojing; Xingyu led forty-five hundred men to the relief, held Jiugong Bridge, fought every day for more than a month until grain and ammunition were nearly exhausted, selected dare-to-die men intending to settle the issue in one battle; then Li Xuyi's relief army arrived, inner and outer forces struck in concert, destroyed three camps adjoining the city, took them in successive days' assault, and the momentum was like splitting bamboo.

In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing; Xingyu led forty-five hundred men to the relief, held Jiugong Bridge, fought every day for more than a month until grain and ammunition were nearly exhausted, selected dare-to-die men intending to settle the issue in one battle; then Li Xuyi's relief army arrived, inner and outer forces struck in concert, destroyed three camps adjoining the city, took them in successive days' assault, and the momentum was like splitting bamboo.
The literal field makes the same place-name error; 寶慶 is Baoqing.
Passing through Wangchao in Zunyi, he found Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Luo Chongguang trapped by bandits.
Passing through Wangchao in Zunyi, he found Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang trapped by bandits.
The governor-general is 勞崇光, Lao Chongguang; the surname 勞 is not Luo.
Passing through Wangchao in Zunyi, he found Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Luo Chongguang besieged by bandits.
Passing through Wangchao in Zunyi, he found Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang besieged by bandits.
The literal field has the same surname error; 勞崇光 is Lao Chongguang.

In the eighth year he captured Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng. For accumulated merit he was promoted to deputy commander with brigadier's rank and granted the titles Shangyong and Zhiyong Batulu.

In the eighth year he captured Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng. For accumulated merit he was promoted to deputy commander with brigadier's rank and granted the titles Shangyong and Zhiyong Baturu.
巴圖魯 is the established Manchu title Baturu in both honorifics named here.

In the eighth year he captured Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng; for accumulated merit he rose to deputy commander, was given the rank of brigadier, and was granted the titles Shangyong and Zhiyong Batulu.

In the eighth year he captured Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng; for accumulated merit he rose to deputy commander, was given the rank of brigadier, and was granted the titles Shangyong and Zhiyong Baturu.
The literal field contains the same title; 巴圖魯 should be rendered Baturu.
Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Luo Chongguang recommended his ability, and he served in succession as acting grain intendant, judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer.
Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang recommended his ability, and he served in succession as acting grain intendant, judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer.
This is another reference to 勞崇光, whose surname is Lao, not Luo.

Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang recommended his talent, and he served in succession as acting grain intendant, provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer.
The literal field repeats the surname error; 勞崇光 is Lao Chongguang.
and ordered Provincial Military Commander Liu Shiji to take Duyun and kill its chief Wu Zhang.
and ordered Provincial Military Commander Liu Shiqi to take Duyun and kill its chief Wu Zhang.
The source gives 劉士奇; 奇 is read qi, so the name is Liu Shiqi rather than Liu Shiji.

and ordered Provincial Military Commander Liu Shiqi to capture Duyun and destroy its chief Wu Zhang.

In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Guangxi. Baotian helped lift the siege of Baojing and was promoted to prefect.
In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Guangxi. Baotian helped lift the siege of Baoqing and was promoted to prefect.
The source again names 寶慶, Baoqing, not Baojing.
In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Guangxi; Baotian followed in lifting the siege of Baojing and was promoted to prefect.
In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Guangxi; Baotian followed in lifting the siege of Baoqing and was promoted to prefect.
The literal field makes the same place-name error; 寶慶 is Baoqing.

In the third year Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again invaded Jiangxi to tie down the Nanjing army. Baotian met them at Baishaguan, seized Jiqiao pass, struck at Dajiguan and Nilingguan, drove the rebels into the hills, recovered Jinxii, was registered as judicial commissioner, and was appointed judicial commissioner of Yunnan.

In the third year Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again invaded Jiangxi to tie down the Nanjing army. Baotian met them at Baishaguan, seized Jiqiao pass, struck at Dajiguan and Nilingguan, drove the rebels into the hills, recovered Jinxi, was registered as judicial commissioner, and was appointed judicial commissioner of Yunnan.
金谿 is Jinxi; the extra final i in Jinxii is a typographical error.

In the third year Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again jointly invaded Jiangxi, intending to pin down the Jiangning army from afar; Baotian met them at Baishaguan, seized the strategic pass at Jiqiao, struck at Dajiguan and Nilingguan, the bandits fled into the mountains, Jinxii was recovered, he was registered by name as provincial judicial commissioner, and was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Yunnan.

In the third year Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again jointly invaded Jiangxi, intending to pin down the Jiangning army from afar; Baotian met them at Baishaguan, seized the strategic pass at Jiqiao, struck at Dajiguan and Nilingguan, the bandits fled into the mountains, Jinxi was recovered, he was registered by name as provincial judicial commissioner, and was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Yunnan.
The literal field contains the same typo; 金谿 is Jinxi.
Runchang and Ziyuan advanced from Sinan, took the Zhenyuan prefectural city, and held it.
Runchang and Ziyuan advanced from Sizhou, took the Zhenyuan prefectural city, and held it.
The point of departure is 思州, Sizhou, not Sinan.
Runchang and Ziyuan advanced from Sinan against the Zhenyuan prefectural city and captured it.
Runchang and Ziyuan advanced from Sizhou against the Zhenyuan prefectural city and captured it.
The literal field repeats the place-name error; 思州 is Sizhou.

Baotian raided Shiling, stormed the rebel stockade, blocked their front with a detachment, and ordered a joint land-and-water attack. Wenjin fled, the siege of Qingyang was raised, and for accumulated merit he received the title Yekenge Batulu and provincial treasurer's rank.

Baotian raided Shiling, stormed the rebel stockade, blocked their front with a detachment, and ordered a joint land-and-water attack. Wenjin fled, the siege of Qingyang was raised, and for accumulated merit he received the title Yekenge Baturu and provincial treasurer's rank.
業鏗額巴圖魯 contains the established Manchu title Baturu, not Batulu.

Baotian raided Shiling, broke the bandit stockade, detached troops to block their front, ordered a joint land-and-water attack, Wenjin fled, the siege of Qingyang was lifted, and for accumulated merit he was granted the title Yekenge Batulu and the rank of provincial treasurer.
